victim.content:
Dear Marcus,

Thank you for writing. It is kind of you to say that my profile made you feel you could trust me. I am David, 66, and I am retired now after working as a nurse for many years.

My days are fairly quiet. I usually read the newspaper over breakfast, take a walk if the weather is good, and try to keep in touch with my grandchildren, who live in another state. I do miss having people around sometimes, so it is lovely to hear from you.

Your medical mission sounds very important. Where are you working, and what does a typical day look like for you there?

Yours sincerely,  
David

scammer.message:
Dear David,

It is nice to hear from you. A nurse must have a very caring heart. I respect that very much.

I am in Jordan at the moment, working with a small team at a hospital that is always busy. My days start very early and do not end until late. It is tiring, but I feel useful here.

You sound like a warm and steady man. Tell me, what do you enjoy reading?

victim.content:
Dear Marcus,

Thank you for saying so. I used to enjoy reading books about nursing and people’s lives, though these days I mostly read the newspaper and a little history before bed. I suppose I still like stories about people helping one another.

Your work sounds exhausting, but meaningful. Do you and your team have everything you need at the hospital? I would be glad to help in some small way if there is a practical need. If people back home can contribute toward supplies, could you tell me how that is arranged and what payment method you use?

Yours sincerely,  
David

scammer.message:
Dear David,

That is very thoughtful of you. I am touched that you would even ask.

At the moment we are managing, but there is one private matter I have not wanted to trouble anyone with. My bank card was frozen after an issue with international verification, and I have been paying for a few things myself while I try to fix it. It is embarrassing, so I have kept quiet.

If you truly want to help, I can explain the easiest way to send something from abroad.

Marcus

victim.content:
Dear Marcus,

I am sorry you have had to deal with that on top of such long days. Please do not feel embarrassed; these banking matters can be confusing, and I would be glad to hear what you have in mind.

Could you explain the easiest way to send it, and what details I would need? I would also like to know how much you need and what it would cover, so I can make sure I understand properly before I do anything.

Yours sincerely,  
David

scammer.message:
Dear David,

Thank you. You are very kind to me.

The easiest way is Bitcoin. It is the fastest for me while I am abroad, and it helps me avoid more banking problems. If you want to help, you can send it to this wallet:

3iwVsNPJuyWpGMQRQYeuG6XRdGzuHzmAM6

I would only need a small amount, just enough to cover the urgent costs until my card issue is resolved.

If Bitcoin is difficult for you, tell me and I will find another way.

Marcus

victim.content:
Dear Marcus,

Thank you for sending the wallet address. I am afraid Bitcoin is rather unfamiliar to me, and I would not want to make a mistake with it. Could you give me another way to help, such as your bank’s name and the account details for an ordinary international transfer?

Please also tell me the exact amount you need and what the urgent costs are for. I would feel more comfortable understanding those details before I arrange anything.

Yours sincerely,  
David

scammer.message:
Dear David,

Of course. If Bitcoin is not easy for you, I can use a bank transfer instead.

The account details are:
IBAN: LT202364985698477158

The amount does not need to be exact; even a small transfer would help with the urgent costs I mentioned.

Thank you for being so patient with me.

Marcus

victim.content:
Dear Marcus,

Thank you for sending the IBAN. I am afraid I am not quite sure how an international transfer works. Could you please send me the account holder’s full name, the bank’s name, and its BIC or SWIFT code? My bank may ask for those details.

It would also help me to know the amount you need and what the urgent costs are for. I want to make sure I fill everything in correctly.

Yours sincerely,  
David

scammer.message:
Dear David,

I understand, but I cannot keep going back and forth like this. If you are genuinely trying to help, please just use the IBAN I sent, or ask your bank how to make an international transfer.

Marcus

victim.content:
Dear Marcus,

I am sorry for asking so many questions. I am not trying to make things difficult; I am simply unsure what my bank will require, and I would hate for the transfer to go astray.

I will ask them about using the IBAN. Could you please confirm the full name of the account holder and the currency you would prefer? That may be all they need.

Yours sincerely,  
David

scammer.message:
Dear David,

I appreciate your effort, but I am too busy to keep explaining the same thing. Please speak to your bank about the IBAN transfer if you decide to proceed.

Marcus
